title: G-L-H
hook: galut, exile, and gilui, revealing, share a root

segments.voice: Yesterday, A-L-M: olam, the world, and ne'elam, hidden. Your line was the world hides. What did you find tucked inside something ordinary? Today, a root where hiding turns into showing. Day one thousand four hundred sixteen.

A letter arrives in Babylon from the prophet Jeremiah, addressed to people carried off from Jerusalem. Other prophets have been promising it'll be over soon. Jeremiah tells them to build houses and live in them, plant gardens and eat what grows, marry, raise children. And then this: "seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace." Pray for the city of your exile. The Hebrew under carried away captives is today's root.
screen: `A LETTER TO BABYLON.` → `BUILD, PLANT, MARRY.` → `SEEK THE PEACE OF THE CITY.`

segments.voice: G-L-H. Gimel, lamed, heh. Galut: exile. Gilui: revealing, uncovering. Turn it a few ways. First, uncovering. The root's plainest sense is to lay something bare. In the book of Ruth, when Boaz wants to tell his relative about Naomi's field, the Hebrew says he wanted to uncover his ear: to let him know. Second, exile. The same letters mean to go into exile, to be carried off. Some readers hear the two meanings as one picture: exile is being uncovered, the covering of home pulled away. Third, God revealed. When Jacob builds an altar at Bethel, the text gives the reason: "because there God appeared unto him, when he fled from the face of his brother." Appeared is from this root, and notice when it happened: while Jacob was running, in his own exile. Deuteronomy draws a line through the root too: "The secret things belong unto the LORD our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever." The revealed is what's handed to people to live by. Fourth, the rabbis. The Talmud teaches that wherever Israel was exiled, the Shechinah, God's presence, went with them. In this root, being sent away and being shown something share their letters. Jeremiah's letter is itself a revelation, mailed into an exile.
screen: `TO UNCOVER AN EAR.` · `EXILE: THE COVERING PULLED AWAY.` · `GOD APPEARED TO JACOB AS HE FLED.` · `THE PRESENCE WENT INTO EXILE TOO.` · then, large: `EXILE REVEALS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: learn from one exile. Settle, and breathe. Bring back a time you were out of place. A move to a new city, a new school, a hospital stay, a family you married into, a room where nobody spoke your language. Let the strangeness return for a moment. Then ask what it showed you that you couldn't have seen at home. Something about yourself, about kindness, about what you need. Hold that one thing. If you pray, you can remember Jeremiah's letter and pray for the place you're in now. The bell holds the time.
screen: `ONE TIME YOU WERE OUT OF PLACE.` · `WHAT DID IT SHOW YOU?` · `HOLD THAT ONE THING.`

segments.voice: G-L-H. Gimel, lamed, heh: galut, exile, and gilui, revealing. To be uncovered, and to be shown. Today's word.
Your line: exile reveals. Today, find one person who's far from home, and ask them one thing they've learned there. Day one thousand four hundred sixteen.

howItsDone: Jewish teaching links galut, exile, and gilui, revealing, through the root gimel-lamed-heh; Jeremiah's letter to the exiles (Jeremiah 29) and the Talmud's teaching that the Shechinah went into exile with Israel (Megillah 29a) can be studied together.
